To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the formal model of the security and safety critical area of aviation is incomplete and does not cover the insider threat.
the current security controls in airplanes against insider threat are not sufficient and that there are no policies that can guarantee safety and security in the presence of insider threat.
there is no way to prevent an insider from intentionally crashing a plane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
(1) how the formal modeling can support security analysis of infrastructures and (2) what are the social factors that are relevant for insider threats in aviation.
the following question: What are the limits of logical modeling for the analysis of security and safety-critical infrastructures?
the limits of formal methods in security and safety-critical systems and with the use of social explanations to fill the gaps in formal modeling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current security controls in airplanes are insufficient to prevent an insider threat from causing a crash.
it is possible to model the security controls and procedures of airplanes, but it is not possible to model the people and their actions.

the Germanwings incident was not caused by a lack of security controls or policies, but rather by a combination of the copilot's psychological state, a lack of security awareness, the security controls and security policies, and the design of the airplane itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is no single solution for the analysis of such threats and that the application of formal methods is not the only way to analyze such threats, although it can be useful for certain parts of the analysis.
the formal analysis of security policies and the application of logical modeling in Isabelle is useful for identifying weaknesses in security policies and procedures.
the current security and safety policies and controls are not sufficient to protect against insider threats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of security controls against insider threats requires social explanation.
logical modeling is not a panacea and that it is important to consider social explanation when analyzing the security and safety of infrastructures.
logical modeling can be useful for identifying and explaining the limits of formal analysis in the context of security and safety critical infrastructures.
